source: products.md in this folder (labels and US list prices read from each maker's own website on 7 October 2026) and lib/ingredient-pages/creatine.ts

lines.text: Which creatine powder is actually worth buying in 2026? We read the labels and list prices on ten makers' own websites. Here are seven, counted down, with the cost a day and the catch for each.
lines.say: Which creatine powder is actually worth buying in twenty twenty-six? We read the labels and list prices on ten makers' own websites. Here are seven, counted down, with the cost a day and the catch for each.

lines.text: First, how we ranked them. Plain creatine monohydrate is the best studied form, and no fancier form has beaten it. The dose is 3 to 5 grams a day. So we compared the cost of 5 grams a day, and whether the tub is independently tested.
lines.say: First, how we ranked them. Plain creatine monohydrate is the best studied form, and no fancier form has beaten it. The dose is three to five grams a day. So we compared the cost of five grams a day, and whether the tub is independently tested.

lines.text: Number seven. Kaged Creatine HCl. It is batch tested by Informed Sport. But it is a different form, and the tub holds only 56 grams. At the label's own dose, that is about $1.33 a day.
lines.say: Number seven. Kaged Creatine H C L. It is batch tested by Informed Sport. But it is a different form, and the tub holds only fifty-six grams. At the label's own dose, that is about a dollar thirty-three a day.

lines.text: Number six. Transparent Labs Creatine HMB. 5 grams of monohydrate, plus HMB and vitamin D. It is certified by Informed Choice. But it costs about $1.67 a day, for extras you may not need.
lines.say: Number six. Transparent Labs Creatine H M B. Five grams of monohydrate, plus H M B and vitamin D. It is certified by Informed Choice. But it costs about a dollar sixty-seven a day, for extras you may not need.

lines.text: Number five, and the best for tested athletes. Thorne Creatine. Plain monohydrate, 5 grams a scoop, and NSF Certified for Sport. The catch is the price: about 49 cents a day.
lines.say: Number five, and the best for tested athletes. Thorne Creatine. Plain monohydrate, five grams a scoop, and N S F Certified for Sport. The catch is the price: about forty-nine cents a day.

lines.text: Number four, the big name. Optimum Nutrition Micronized Creatine. 5 grams a scoop, and the page says banned substance tested, without naming the tester. About 27 cents a day in the 120 serving tub.
lines.say: Number four, the big name. Optimum Nutrition Micronized Creatine. Five grams a scoop, and the page says banned substance tested, without naming the tester. About twenty-seven cents a day in the hundred and twenty serving tub.

lines.text: Number three. Nutricost Creatine Monohydrate. Simple and cheap: about 24 cents a day in the 500 gram tub. It says third party tested, but shows no sport certification.
lines.say: Number three. Nutricost Creatine Monohydrate. Simple and cheap: about twenty-four cents a day in the five hundred gram tub. It says third party tested, but shows no sport certification.

lines.text: Number two, and the cheapest. BulkSupplements Creatine Monohydrate. The 1 kilogram bag works out at about 15 cents a day. The catch: we saw no sport certification, and the label suggests 7 grams a day. 3 to 5 is enough.
lines.say: Number two, and the cheapest. Bulk Supplements Creatine Monohydrate. The one kilogram bag works out at about fifteen cents a day. The catch: we saw no sport certification, and the label suggests seven grams a day. Three to five is enough.

lines.text: And number one. NOW Sports Creatine Monohydrate. Plain monohydrate, 5 grams a serving, certified by Informed Sport, at about 21 cents a day in the 1 kilogram tub. It is not the cheapest. It is the cheapest we found with a named sport certification.
lines.say: And number one. Now Sports Creatine Monohydrate. Plain monohydrate, five grams a serving, certified by Informed Sport, at about twenty-one cents a day in the one kilogram tub. It is not the cheapest. It is the cheapest we found with a named sport certification.

lines.chapter: Cost a day, side by side
lines.text: Side by side, at 5 grams a day. 15 cents. 21. 24. 27. 49. Then well over a dollar for the two at the bottom.
lines.say: Side by side, at five grams a day. Fifteen cents. Twenty-one. Twenty-four. Twenty-seven. Forty-nine. Then well over a dollar for the two at the bottom.

lines.text: Whichever you buy, the method is the same. 3 to 5 grams a day, every day, at any time. Loading is optional. And skip the gummies: plain powder is the most reliable way to get a known dose.
lines.say: Whichever you buy, the method is the same. Three to five grams a day, every day, at any time. Loading is optional. And skip the gummies: plain powder is the most reliable way to get a known dose.

lines.text: Creatine is safe for healthy adults. But speak to a doctor first if you have kidney disease, or are pregnant or breastfeeding.
lines.say: Creatine is safe for healthy adults. But speak to a doctor first if you have kidney disease, or are pregnant or breastfeeding.

lines.text: The bottom line. For most people: NOW Sports. On a tight budget: BulkSupplements. If you are drug tested: Thorne. Prices change, so check the cost a day before you buy. Links are in the description. This is general information, not medical advice.
